page: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v6 is a general-purpose instance powered by 64 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores operating at a base frequency of 3.4 GHz. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides a 1:1 mapping of 64 virtual CPUs to 64 physical cores with no simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via hardware-level AES support. The instance includes no bundled local disk storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a pronounced divergence between single-threaded and parallelized compute performance. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, place the Neoverse-N2 cores in the middle 50% percentile. In contrast, parallel workloads scale effectively across the dedicated cores, yielding top-tier results in multi-core stress tests, Geekbench multi-core runs, and Clang software compilation. The memory architecture exhibits top-tier throughput, sustaining uncached large-block read rates of 463.82 GB/sec and write rates of 203.11 GB/sec. Synthetic database metrics and static web serving throughput also register in the top 10%, while in-memory operations demonstrate strong throughput in Redis SET tests.

Qualitatively, the D64ps_v6 provides high resource density for scale-out architectures, delivering strong throughput per compute unit across highly parallel workloads. Key technical tradeoffs involve the absence of bundled local storage, requiring attached network storage volumes for stateful operations, and modest per-core throughput that may throttle single-thread-bound tasks. This virtual machine is structurally aligned with large-scale multi-threaded compilation pipelines, static web delivery clusters, caching tiers, microservices backends, and containerized microservice platforms.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on 64 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 physical cores running at 3.4 GHz, paired with 256 GB of system memory. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an architecture with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, 128 MB of L3 cache, and hardware AES acceleration, but includes no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark testing reveals average single-core performance alongside top-tier multi-threaded execution, demonstrating exceptional throughput in multi-core stress tests, Clang software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. Memory subsystem performance is also top-tier, delivering over 463 GB/sec in large-block reads and robust database operations. Cost efficiency is driven by the density of dedicated 64-core ARM silicon, providing high parallelism per resource unit. However, applications requiring intense single-thread burst speed or bundled local NVMe storage will need remote storage attachment. The instance is well suited for static web serving, multi-threaded backend processing, CI/CD compilation, and in-memory caches.
